hooks.name: buff.Buff.Reset
hooks.semanticRole: Buff definition/instance lifecycle or explicitly assigned action entry
hooks.evidenceBoundary: Direct method entry, supplied arguments and separate pre-entry stored carriers only. Raw receiver and reference-argument slots retain same-process pointer identities. Reset entry caches may belong to the previous pooled instance. Return values, actual writes, action completion, collection contents, targets, blackboard evaluation and server acceptance are not observed. A live ownership join requires an explicit Reset/ReAssign environment argument, matching receiver identities and lifecycle boundaries; timestamp proximity is insufficient.

coverageGaps: Reset and _LoadActions have stack arguments; NewAction has a reference return; generic assignment and Ability.Init stay entry-only.
Paired consumers preserve Boolean return bits and same-path before/after fields; return success does not establish downstream or server effects.
Entry/return snapshots are sequential, bounded and non-atomic; unreadable fields, transport losses or incomplete pairs withhold affected claims.
No per-frame trigger capture, live collection enumeration, formatter-provider binding, raw serialized cursor, evaluated blackboard or final HP write.
Source snapshots are retained export context, not evidence that a specific serialized node was selected by the runtime.
The withdrawn anonymous assignment hook stays omitted; prepared named ABI and successful build do not establish live hook safety.
A new run cannot replace the missing original Skill source-capture receipt.
SelfRotateAction and BlowOffAction retain only common action state/environment paths; their stored Data slot is omitted because the current generic layout witness refuses their extra instance fields.

Outer AbilityAction.Execute, both SequenceAction execution routes and IfElseAction child-sequence references are observed; unhooked intervening calls, asynchronous ownership and serialized-node selection remain unresolved.

SequenceAction.m_actions collection identity is omitted: the current reference-identity preparer refuses that closed generic reference path. Sequence receiver bits, ordinary scalar guards and IfElse child-sequence references remain selected.
